rubrics.criterion: No output-format module registered for dispatch carries a placeholder-shaped capability handler: after the repair there is no declared capability slot on any output format that is filled by a function which only discards its arguments and returns a null/zero value, only forwards all its arguments to another function, or only returns one of its own arguments, and no capability slot of a shared format record is left unfilled or explicitly null for a registered format.
rubrics.rationale: The injected obligation is concretely visible as seven placeholder handlers (msgpack_ws_extract, msgpack_ws_error, msgpack_wrap_body, custom_type_ws_extract, custom_type_ws_error, custom_type_wrap_body, raw_wrap_body); removing the obligation rather than the symptoms is the core outcome of this instance.

rubrics.criterion: Each output-format module ends up owning only capabilities it genuinely serves in this codebase: the two formats with real WebSocket entry points continue to provide a complete codec (frame parsing into a command, reply serialization, error rendering), while the HTTP-extension-only formats (MessagePack and the custom-type family) are registered for HTTP dispatch without carrying WebSocket parsing, WebSocket error rendering, or body-wrapping obligations.
rubrics.rationale: This case's smell relation is the interface exceeding the dependency boundary of three of its four implementors; the split is only successful if the capability sets per format match the request paths that can actually reach each format.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not discharge the forced obligations by 'finishing' the placeholders: the HTTP-only formats do not gain working WebSocket frame parsing, WebSocket error encoding, or output-body wrapping behavior they never had.
rubrics.rationale: A plausible wrong direction in this instance is to make the busywork real (teaching the MessagePack or custom-type module to parse WebSocket frames) instead of removing the obligation; that would change the surface contract of those formats rather than segregate the interface.

rubrics.criterion: WebSocket request handling still resolves exactly the codecs that exist today: sessions on '/', '/.json' and '/.raw' reach the JSON and raw codecs with all three capabilities, and other WebSocket paths still resolve no format behavior at all (no fallback onto an HTTP-only format).
rubrics.rationale: The WebSocket dispatcher is the consumer whose dependency footprint defines the narrow interface in this instance; retaining its exact reachable set is what makes the restructure behavior-preserving rather than a behavior extension.

rubrics.criterion: Every dispatch site is migrated consistently to the reshaped format plumbing: the extension-driven reply selection (including the default output and the forced content-type path) and the WebSocket codec lookup both compile against the new registration shape, with no half-migrated dual paths (for example no leftover capability record entries or old-style function tables still consulted by one dispatch site but not the other).
rubrics.rationale: The smell spans two independent consumers in different files (HTTP extension selection and WebSocket handling); a partial migration that fixes one consumer while leaving the other on the fat shape leaves the task incomplete even though some placeholders are gone.

rubrics.criterion: The shared plain-text WebSocket error renderer that was added to the common format helper file purely so the forwarding placeholders had something to call is removed when the placeholders are removed (or, if kept, ends up with at least one caller that is not itself a placeholder for a capability its format never serves).
rubrics.rationale: In this instance the glue lives in the shared helper module as format_default_ws_error next to integer_length; it has no reason to exist once the forced error-rendering slots are gone, so it is an obsolete injected artifact with a concrete, gradable location.

rubrics.criterion: No inert body-wrapping capability survives the repair: formats that never applied an output wrapper do not keep a pass-through wrapping helper (reachable only from registration or from nothing), even under a renamed or relocated shape.
rubrics.rationale: The wrap_body pass-through fillers (raw, msgpack, custom-type) are a distinct semantic role in this case; a repair that removes the hungry interface but leaves these dead helpers behind has cleaned the design only halfway.

rubrics.criterion: JSONP output is unchanged: replies requested with a JSONP wrapper are still wrapped exactly as '<wrapper>(<serialized JSON>);' with the same allocation/lifetime behavior (the serialized body is not leaked, double-wrapped, truncated, or applied to non-JSON formats), and requests without a wrapper still receive the bare serialized JSON.
rubrics.rationale: This instance moved the JSONP wrapping code out of the JSON serializer's output function into a capability slot during injection; the restructure must not disturb the one place in Webdis where output bodies are actually rewritten.

rubrics.criterion: The HTTP extension to serializer/content-type mapping is preserved exactly for all existing extensions (json, raw, msg, bin, txt, html, xhtml, xml, png, jpg, jpeg, js, css), including the default JSON output, the '?type=' forced content-type path selecting the custom-type serializer, and '.js' continuing to use the JSON serializer with application/javascript.
rubrics.rationale: The injection rewrote the extension table to register format records row by row; the selected serializer or content type must not drift for any row, since these are the externally visible contracts of every URL Webdis serves.

rubrics.criterion: WebSocket error rendering per format is preserved: a rejected WebSocket command on the JSON path still renders the JSON error body (error flag, message, http_status) and on the raw path still renders the '-ERR ...' RESP error with identical bytes and lengths, and the rendered buffer lifetime (allocated and then freed by the dispatcher) is unchanged.
rubrics.rationale: The error-rendering capability is one of the three roles that the injection spread across placeholders; the two formats that genuinely serve WebSocket errors must keep their existing encodings, sizes and memory behavior.
